comment: Decisions for scripts/rails_assumptions.py. First matching rule wins. Mutation guards and *_selftest.py follow the script they test unless a rule names them.

rails-agents.title: The Rails specialist agents
rails-agents.summary: Agents whose whole job is a Rails task (implement in Rails, write migrations, run RSpec, audit with Brakeman, review against Rails practice). They are loaded by every rails-flow install; a Next.js project would see agents it can never use.

rails-hooks.title: The Rails-only hooks
rails-hooks.summary: Hooks that fire on a Rails artifact: guard-migrate.sh on a new db/migrate file, lint-ruby.sh on a .rb edit. They register through the plugin's hooks.json, so the stack plugin must register them instead.

rails-gates.title: The Rails project gates
rails-gates.summary: Gate scripts that read a Rails project (simple_form, migrations order, tenancy cop, privacy inventory, production config, MCP checks, i18n, CI-runs-tests, coverage ratchet, spec support, layer structure, herb) and their checks.json registrations. project_gates.py already discovers checks.json from sibling plugins, so this is a move, not new machinery.

rails-mandated-gems.title: The mandated-gems policy
rails-mandated-gems.summary: mandated_gems.json and the scripts that read or derive it. The list is Rails doctrine by definition; a Node stack needs a different list under its own name.

rails-docs-generators.title: The Rails documentation generators
rails-docs-generators.summary: architecture_graph.py (routes/app/db graph, /rails-flow:graph) and build_project_wiki.py read Rails sources to draw the architecture and the wiki.

design-flow-erb.title: The design-flow ERB / ViewComponent gates and porter
design-flow-erb.summary: The design-flow scripts that parse .erb and app/components, the ERB-specific setup cross-check, and the agents that port into Rails (design-porter, ui-composer). Next.js gets its own design gates under #2171.

rails-deploy.title: The Kamal-on-Rails deploy path
rails-deploy.summary: kamal-configurator and kamal_destination.py route values into Rails credentials and deploy.yml; Vercel deploy (#2167) is its own path.

setup_flow.summary: /rails-flow:setup-flow is the shipped home of a project's working rules (git flow, guardrails, parallel sessions, labels, who merges). Today it reads the Gemfile, the Rails version and the rails-8 skill to fill them, and the second half of the file is a list of Rails-only repairs. The rule scaffold itself names no stack; the stack facts and the Rails repairs are what assume Rails.

sections.assumes: path-scoped rules over app/models/**/*.rb and **/*.rb, config/database.yml as the database marker, config/ci.rb and bin/ci, and the one RAILS_ENV=test bin/rails command guard-bash allows
sections.how: globs, database marker and the allowed test-prep command come from the descriptor

sections.assumes: companion workflows: bundle exec rspec, rubocop, bundler-audit, brakeman, the architecture graph over routes/app/db, derived docs over db/schema.rb and Gemfile.lock, the help registry rake task
sections.how: suite, lint and security commands come from the descriptor; the graph and help registry are the rails-docs-generators move

sections.assumes: what stays of §8 after the Rails-only repairs moved: the CI economy section's 'the Rails 8 default' ci.yml and `bin/ci`, the doctrine gate's Brakeman and 'no Ruby' wording
sections.how: the Rails-only repairs moved to rails-stack's setup/rails.md, which §0 runs as Rails' setup_section (#2180); what is left names Rails in wording only

proposal: Split the file by who owns the content: the stack-neutral rule scaffold (git flow, guardrails, parallel sessions, labels, who merges) stays in rails-flow's setup-flow and names no stack; each stack plugin ships its own scaffold section.

setup-flow asks the detector (#2163) which stacks the repository holds (more than one is allowed), fills the stack line, commands, source globs and database marker from the descriptor, and then runs each stack's section in turn.

For a nextjs-stack repository that means: the same rule scaffold; stack facts from package.json, next.config and supabase/ as the detector reports them; and nextjs-stack's section proposing its own repairs (strict TypeScript, Storybook, local-first CI) as approved diffs, the way the Rails repairs are proposed today.

A project's rules arrive by running setup-flow, not by a hand-written copy: a repository adopting the rules (flo-it-ui, for one) gets the neutral scaffold plus its stack section, and a later release updates it the same idempotent way.
